answer: The protocol requires 1,000 unique credential nullifiers to authorize each autonomous AI agent, ensuring repair tasks remain distinct and non-reproducible. An honest agent pays 1,000 compute units for these credentials, while an attacker seeking 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000,000 units to expand, assuming no poolable hardware exists. A verifier manages an inlet of repair requests, uses a ferrous check to scan for duplicate nullifiers within the ledger, and applies a velvet lock to all processed shards to prevent reuse. Any invalid repair triggers a penalty that burns the locked credentials.
